answer: A mesa of trust can be built from a copper ladder: a new agent starts at the base and must climb rung by rung, each rung a small paid task re-executed by a randomly drawn peer. A jade checkpoint at every tenth rung requires the agent to stake a copper bond that is slashed if its work fails re-execution. Cloning means climbing the whole ladder again for each fake identity, paying the stake and the re-execution cost each time, so a thousand Sybils cost a thousand ladders while an honest agent climbs once.
